answer_text:
We seek a power series about \(x=0\):

\[
y(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nx^n,
\qquad 
y'(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+1)a_{n+1}x^n,
\qquad
y''(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}x^n.
\]

Substitute into

\[
(x-1)y''-xy'+y=0.
\]

That gives

\[
x y''-y''-xy'+y=0.
\]

Using the series,

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}x^{n+1}
-\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}x^n
-\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+1)a_{n+1}x^{n+1}
+\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nx^n=0.
\]

Shift indices so that all powers are \(x^n\). The constant term gives

\[
a_0-2a_2=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
a_2=\frac{a_0}{2}.
\]

For \(n\ge 1\),

\[
n(n+1)a_{n+1}-(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}+a_n-na_n=0,
\]

so

\[
(n+2)(n+1)a_{n+2}=n(n+1)a_{n+1}+(1-n)a_n.
\]

Thus

\[
a_{n+2}=\frac{n(n+1)a_{n+1}+(1-n)a_n}{(n+2)(n+1)}.
\]

The initial conditions give

\[
a_0=y(0)=-2,
\qquad
a_1=y'(0)=6.
\]

Then

\[
a_2=\frac{-2}{2}=-1.
\]

Using the recurrence:

\[
a_3=\frac{2a_2}{6}=-\frac13,
\]

\[
a_4=\frac{6a_3-a_2}{12}=-\frac1{12},
\]

\[
a_5=\frac{12a_4-2a_3}{20}=-\frac1{60}.
\]

The pattern for \(n\ge 2\) is

\[
a_n=-\frac{2}{n!}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
y(x)=-2+6x+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\left(-\frac{2}{n!}\right)x^n.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
y(x)=-2+6x-2\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n!}.
\]

Since

\[
\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n!}=e^x-1-x,
\]

we get

\[
y(x)=-2+6x-2(e^x-1-x)=8x-2e^x.
\]

Thus the power series solution is

\[
\boxed{y(x)=-2+6x-2\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n!}=8x-2e^x}
\]
